title: Magnetic gripper, gripping row, gripping system and gripping row system

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0014) The reference describes a magnetic gripper (housing) with a contact surface (workpiece contact surface) for gripping a battery cell (workpiece). It also mentions a displaceable magnet.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The magnet can be moved between an active (gripping) and passive (release) state by displacement along the longitudinal axis.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The reference describes an 'Anlageabschnitt' (contact section) made of magnetizable material that provides the contact surface. This functions as a pole shoe, but it does not explicitly state 'pole shoes' in plural or that each pole shoe has a contact surface, rather a single contact surface is mentioned.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0016) The magnetizable contact section (acting as a pole shoe) is described as being penetrated by the magnetic field to apply magnetic force to the workpiece at the contact surface, indicating it guides the field.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0014) The contact surface is perpendicular to the longitudinal axis, and the magnet displacement is parallel to this axis. This means the contact surface is at 90 degrees to the displacement direction, which is 180 degrees relative to the workpiece's approach direction, falling within the 170-190 degree range.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The magnetic gripper has a housing, a displaceable magnet, and a contact surface (pole shoe) that is perpendicular to the longitudinal axis, which is the direction of magnet displacement. This implies a 180-degree angle relative to the displacement direction, which is within the specified range.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0016) In the active (gripping) state, the magnet's field penetrates the contact surface, applying a magnetic force to the battery cell (ferromagnetic workpiece) towards the contact surface.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The magnet is displaced along the longitudinal axis of the magnetic gripper, meaning the displacement direction is parallel to the longitudinal axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The reference describes a magnetizable contact section that provides the contact surface and guides the magnetic field. However, it does not explicitly mention an 'active structure' beyond the material composition and general function of guiding the field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: Each centering element has an 'Einführungsschräge' (bevel) for guiding the battery cell to the contact surface. This bevel forms an angle of 15° with the direction of extension of the centering elements, which is parallel to the longitudinal axis and thus perpendicular to the contact surface. This 15° angle is within the 5-85° range.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at abstract) The centering elements are described as projections ('Auskragungen') that guide the workpiece. They are made of non-magnetizable material, so they do not direct the magnetic field, but they do define the space around the contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference describes multiple centering elements as projections, but does not discuss recesses between them or their dimensions relative to projection length.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0002) The centering elements act as a positioning device to guide and center the battery cell (workpiece) on the contact surface.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: The reference describes a single 'Anlageabschnitt' (contact section) providing the contact surface, not distinct first and second pole shoes with opposite polarities.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.note: The magnet is pneumatically displaceable, as indicated by the use of compressed air connections to switch between active (gripping) and passive (release) states.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0006) The magnetic gripper can have presence sensors to detect if the battery cell (workpiece) is at or on the contact surface.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0020) The housing has grooves ('Nuten') designed to receive a sensor and/or a supply line.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0019) The magnetic gripper has an adapter plate with a manipulator interface for attaching to a manipulator, for example via a screw connection.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not describe any housing portion or shielding device specifically designed to suppress or prevent magnetic field escape.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference describes projections (centering elements) but does not provide any dimensions or relationships between their length and the workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0020) The housing has grooves ('Nuten') that serve as receptacles for sensors and/or supply lines.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: Each centering element has a bevel ('Einführungsschräge') that forms an angle of 15° with the direction of extension of the centering elements. This direction is perpendicular to the contact surface, so the bevel angle with the contact surface is 15°, which is within the 15-75° range.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference explicitly states a bevel angle of 15°, which is outside the 40-60° range.

claims.note: (non-English passage at abstract) The reference discloses a magnetic gripper for gripping a battery cell, which is a type of ferromagnetic workpiece.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The reference describes a magnet that can be shifted along a longitudinal axis between an active (gripping) and passive (release) state.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The reference discloses a contact surface provided by a magnetizable section, which acts similarly to a pole shoe to guide magnetic flux. However, it does not explicitly mention multiple 'pole shoes' but rather a single 'Anlageabschnitt' (contact section) that provides the 'Anlagefläche' (contact surface).
The reference does not describe a contact surface defining a specific contact surface angle with respect to a displacement direction, nor does it provide any angular ranges for such a feature.
The reference describes an Anlagefläche (contact surface) but does not specify a contact surface angle or a range for it.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0014) The reference states that the contact surface is perpendicular to a longitudinal axis of the magnetic gripper, implying the housing extends along this axis.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The reference states the magnet is displaceable along the longitudinal axis, which implies the displacement direction is parallel to the longitudinal axis. However, the claim refers to a 'displacement direction' for the magnet, while the reference refers to the magnet being 'displaceable along the longitudinal axis'.
The reference does not describe pole shoes having an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
(non-English passage at claim 6) This passage discloses that each centering element has an introduction bevel for guiding the battery cell to the contact surface.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0018) This passage discloses that the bevel and a direction form an angle, but it does not explicitly state that the bevel and the workpiece contact surface define a bevel angle.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0018) This passage discloses a specific angle of 15 degrees between the bevel and a direction, which falls within the claimed range of 5° to 85°, but it does not explicitly state that this is the bevel angle with the workpiece contact surface, nor does it list the other ranges.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0002) This passage discloses that the centering elements guide and center the battery cell to the contact surface, which is analogous to directing a magnetic field portion and forming a workpiece contact surface, but it does not explicitly mention directing a magnetic field portion or forming the workpiece contact surface.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0002) The reference discloses a plurality of centering elements, which are projections, and specifies that there can be 3, 4, or 6 of them, thus implying at least a first and a second projection.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0017) The reference states that the centering elements are arranged crown-like around the contact surface and surround it in a radial direction, which implies that individual projections are adjacent to one another.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0017) The reference describes the centering elements defining a receiving space and an opening for the battery cell, which inherently creates recesses between the projections.
The reference does not provide any specific dimensions or relationships between the depth/length of recesses and the length of the projections, nor does it mention a deviation percentage.
The reference describes a magnetic gripper for battery cells with centering elements, but does not mention a separate positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece on a workpiece contact surface.
The reference describes a magnet and centering elements, but does not mention pole shoes, let alone a first and second pole shoe.
The reference describes a magnet providing a magnetic effect but does not specify pole shoes acting as north and south poles in a gripping position.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0015) The quote discloses that the magnet is displaceable between an active (gripping) and passive (release) state by shifting it. However, it only mentions pneumatic actuation for this displacement, not electrical or mechanical actuation.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0006) The reference discloses a presence sensor for detecting if the battery cell is at the contact surface, which is related to detecting a gripping position, but does not explicitly mention detecting a release position.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0006) The reference discloses a presence sensor to detect if the battery cell (workpiece) is at the contact surface, which functions as a workpiece sensor.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) The reference discloses a groove (Nut) in the magnetic gripper for receiving a sensor and/or a supply line, which can be considered a receptacle in the housing.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0009) The reference explicitly discloses a manipulator interface for attaching the magnetic gripper to a manipulator.
The reference does not describe a housing portion designed to suppress the escape of the magnetic field.
The reference does not describe a shielding device to prevent the magnetic field from escaping the housing.
(non-English passage at paragraph p0012) This passage describes a gripping system comprising a magnetic gripper and a battery cell.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0012) The reference discloses a magnetic gripper and a battery cell, but the claim specifies a 'ferromagnetic workpiece' which is a broader term than 'Batteriezelle' (battery cell), and the reference does not explicitly state the workpiece is ferromagnetic, although it implies it for magnetic gripping.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0016) This passage describes the active state where the magnet applies a magnetic force to the battery cell against the contact surface, which is equivalent to the gripping state and the workpiece being pressed against the contact surface.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0016) This passage describes the passive state where the magnetic field does not apply a magnetic force greater than the weight of the battery cell, which corresponds to the release state where the workpiece is not pressed by magnetic force.
The reference describes the length of the centering elements and their angle, but does not relate their length to the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece with a specific percentage deviation.

(non-English passage at paragraph p0011) This passage explicitly states that the magnetic gripper can have a groove (Nut) for receiving a sensor and/or a supply line, and that the groove can act as a cable duct, which is a form of receptacle.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet, a contact surface, and centering elements for gripping battery cells, disclosing many core features of the subject invention, including the magnet's displacement, positioning elements, and manipulator interface.
